A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same ActionParty paper, with 23 pages including supplementary Sections A-E. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison establish complete comparability; differences are confined to the first-page arXiv stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original Melting Pot experiments, baseline comparisons, and component ablations in Section 4, with additional results in supplementary Tables 5-6.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and results, including ActionParty's movement accuracy of 0.779 in Table 1 and the ablations in Table 3.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains identical joint video/state denoising, attention masks, spatial RoPE biasing, and autoregressive training and inference procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same 46 Melting Pot games, Coins ablations, and reported long-horizon and variable-player-count tests in supplementary Section D.

E2.justification: Pretrained AR, Zero-shot I2V, and Text-Action remain the comparators in Tables 1-2 and 5-6. The Veo 3 comparison in Figure 1 is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Both retain the same training budgets, 2,000 training videos per game, 230 evaluation rollouts, metrics, sampling procedures, and separate Coins ablation protocol in Sections 4.1 and 4.3.

E4.justification: The attention-mask and RoPE ablations, autoregressive stability analysis, subject-count breakdowns, and generalization observations are identical in Section 4 and supplementary Sections A and D.

E5.justification: Both use the same point-estimate reporting. Neither reports repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results match, including movement accuracy 0.779 and FVD 17.16 in Table 1, overall effect accuracy 0.861 in Table 2, and supplementary Tables 5-6.

T1.justification: The problem definitions, spatial-state assumptions, conditional distributions in Equations 1-2, and mathematical description of RoPE are unchanged. Neither version adds proofs or theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical contributions and claims about action binding, subject consistency, and controlling up to seven subjects across 46 environments.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and limitations are identical, including coordinate drift, disappearing subjects, imperfect generalization, lack of real-time operation, and the restriction to 2D game experiments.

D1.justification: Implementation details, coordinate encoding, data preparation, prompt formats, and the project-site link remain identical in Section 4.1 and supplementary Sections B-C. The updated arXiv version link adds no reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 2 and all 94 reference entries are unchanged, including the positioning relative to Multiverse, Solaris, and MultiGen.

P1.justification: Only the first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 2 April 2026 to v2 dated 30 July 2026. The paper's wording, headings, terminology, and organization are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: The first-page arXiv margin stamp changes placement and spacing. All figures, tables, captions, and body layout remain unchanged; pages 2-23 render identically.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, and appendices are identical. Updating and repositioning the arXiv stamp produces no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
